title: Selecting and Governing a Cloud Provider
context: Your organization is outsourcing the hosting of a critical application. You must lead the selection, sign the right documents, and organize ongoing monitoring.

n1.text: Before contacting vendors, what do you do first?

choices.text: Define the requirements and conduct due diligence (security, compliance, jurisdiction)
choices.why: Scoped requirements and due diligence govern all subsequent choices.

choices.text: Immediately sign an NDA with the first vendor available
choices.why: Confidentiality does not replace evaluating the candidate and the requirements.

choices.text: Request an RFQ before knowing what is expected
choices.why: A price quote requires a service that is already precisely defined.

n2.text: The selected vendor agrees to a master agreement. How do you describe the specific hosting engagement?

choices.text: In a SOW attached to the MSA, with deliverables, scope, and schedule
choices.why: The MSA carries the general terms; the SOW describes each engagement.

choices.text: In a single MOU, without deliverable details
choices.why: An MOU expresses intent; it does not define an operational engagement.

choices.text: In an RFI sent after signing
choices.why: An RFI is an upstream information-gathering document, not a contractual document.

n3.text: Six months later, recovery times degrade. What is the best response?

choices.text: Measure SLAs, request an attestation, and plan an exit clause
choices.why: Contractual tracking, compliance proof, and reversibility address the drift.

choices.text: Increase the budget without modifying the contract
choices.why: Paying more without contractual leverage does not fix the breach.
Vendor lock-in can make an abrupt exit riskier than the drift.

n4.outcome: You scoped the selection, structured MSA/SOW, and implemented contractual monitoring with a controlled exit.

debrief: Selection starts with requirements and due diligence, not price.
MSA = general terms; SOW = specific engagement; SLA/SLO = expected performance.
Continuous monitoring and reversibility limit third-party risk over time.
